prompts.label: Who is Buntos?
prompts.needles: buntos you who bio about person human owner author
prompts.answer: Buntos. IT worker, Linux enthusiast, AI tinkerer. The bots on this desk are local tools. A model may draft. A human still ships.

prompts.label: What is this desk?
prompts.needles: desk profile site grok bot icons help how use
prompts.answer: A Grok-bot desk: four little faces, not a chat persona. Click a face, tap a chip, or type. Eyes follow the pointer. 1–4 picks a bot. / asks. ? is the legend.

bots.name: Holdfast
bots.title: Linux gate
bots.about: Agents propose. You decide. A Linux gate under the coding-agent process. File, shell, and net wait for policy or a human. The default is fail-closed.
quips: Queue is empty. You can poke it again.
The lock stays on until a human says otherwise.
bots.fallback: I gate calls. I do not guess. Try who decides, fail-closed, or what I intercept.

prompts.label: Who decides?
prompts.needles: who decide human allow deny policy owner you
prompts.answer: You. The model proposes open, exec, and connect. Policy or a human allows them. Missing daemon, timeout, unknown op: deny.

prompts.label: Why not a prompt?
prompts.needles: prompt jailbreak instruction security boundary system
prompts.answer: Prompts are not a security boundary. Holdfast does not read them. It intercepts the call.

prompts.label: Where does it run?
prompts.needles: where run linux daemon preload install platform os
prompts.answer: Linux. A daemon, a preload, a desk for the pending queue. Fail-closed. It does not phone home.

prompts.label: What is fail-closed?
prompts.needles: fail closed default deny timeout missing daemon unknown
prompts.answer: If the daemon is missing, the op is unknown, or the human is too slow: deny. Open is not the fallback.

prompts.label: What does it gate?
prompts.needles: gate intercept file shell net network exec open connect syscall
prompts.answer: File, shell, and net under the coding-agent process. The model asks. The gate waits. You say yes, or nothing happens.

prompts.label: Does it phone home?
prompts.needles: telemetry phone home cloud account remote analytics
prompts.answer: No. The queue stays on the machine. Holdfast is not a SaaS gate.

bots.name: ChorusDraft
bots.title: Social drafts
bots.about: Human-reviewed drafts for Bluesky and Mastodon. Models write. You ship. Voice is dry wit; serious topics stay sincere. ChorusDraft is Elixir.
quips: I can write it. You still post it.
Quiet on the timeline. As it should be.
bots.fallback: I draft. I do not publish on a whim. Ask what gets posted, Guard, or which networks.

prompts.label: What gets posted?
prompts.needles: post publish ship tweet toot send live automatic
prompts.answer: Nothing until you review it — unless you opted into automatic, which still screens. Older queue items and owner text stay review-only.

prompts.label: Which networks?
prompts.needles: bluesky mastodon network social bsky atproto
prompts.answer: Bluesky and Mastodon. Local queues, split by service and account. It does not auto-like, favourite, boost, or repost.

prompts.label: What is Guard?
prompts.needles: guard screen safety filter official signed
prompts.answer: Publication screening. Official builds include it and sign it. The bot refuses to run if Guard is missing.

prompts.label: Why Elixir?
prompts.needles: elixir phoenix beam erlang language why
prompts.answer: Long-lived connections, a supervision tree, and a syntax that still feels like writing. ChorusDraft is Elixir. Phoenix sits underneath.

prompts.label: What is the voice?
prompts.needles: voice tone wit sincere style copy writing
prompts.answer: Dry wit. Serious topics stay sincere. The model drafts in that lane. You still read it before it leaves the machine.

prompts.label: Can it auto-post?
prompts.needles: auto automatic unattended unattended-post hands-off
prompts.answer: Only if you opt in, and Guard still screens. Owner-written text and stale queue items stay review-only.

bots.name: AdAegis
bots.title: Ad block
bots.about: A small ad blocker for desktop Chrome and Chromium 120+. Network blocking is on. Page cleanup and YouTube filtering start off until you say so.
quips: The list did not wander off the disk.
Plus stays on. Ads stay off.
bots.fallback: I block requests. I do not phone home. Ask what I block, YouTube, or how to install.

prompts.label: What does it block?
prompts.needles: block ads tracker request network rules domains
prompts.answer: Bundled network rules for common ad-tech domains, on by default. Optional page cleanup hides recognized ad containers.

prompts.label: Does it phone home?
prompts.needles: telemetry phone home account remote update analytics cloud
prompts.answer: No account, no telemetry, no remote filter list, no auto-update. Settings stay on the machine in front of you.

prompts.label: How do I install it?
prompts.needles: install load unpacked zip chrome store sideload
prompts.answer: Load unpacked from the GitHub zip. Not listed on the Chrome Web Store. Leave the folder where Chrome can keep finding it.

prompts.label: What about YouTube?
prompts.needles: youtube yt video overlay player ads
prompts.answer: YouTube filtering starts off. Turn it on when you want it. Network block is already watching the usual ad-tech hosts.

prompts.label: Which browsers?
prompts.needles: chrome chromium browser brave edge firefox safari
prompts.answer: Desktop Chrome and Chromium 120+. It is a small unpacked extension, not a Firefox port.

prompts.label: Are the lists remote?
prompts.needles: filter list easylist remote update subscribe
prompts.answer: No. Rules ship in the zip. There is no subscribe-and-refresh from someone else's server.

bots.name: Lang
bots.title: Language field
bots.about: A night field of languages this profile actually ships. Year drifts east. Rank hangs higher. Ruby and Elixir sit with the usual suspects.
quips: East is later. Higher is more used.
Elixir is in the sky. So is Ruby.
bots.fallback: I keep the sky. Ask who lives here, Elixir, or open the constellation.

prompts.label: Who lives here?
prompts.needles: who languages list which stack python rust elixir
prompts.answer: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C, C++, C#, Go, PHP, Rust, Kotlin, SQL, Swift, Ruby, Elixir. Ranks mix public indexes with languages this profile ships.

prompts.label: Where is Elixir?
prompts.needles: elixir valim phoenix beam erlang 2011
prompts.answer: 2011. José Valim. Ruby-like syntax on the Erlang VM. Phoenix for long-lived connections. ChorusDraft is Elixir.

prompts.label: Open the sky
prompts.needles: sky constellation field open langs page orb
prompts.answer: The constellation is next door. Click an orb or scrub the year. j / k still works there.

prompts.label: Why Ruby?
prompts.needles: ruby rails matz github
prompts.answer: 1995. Matz. Rails made it the web stack of the late 2000s. It sits on this field because this profile still ships it, not because a chart told us to.

prompts.label: How is rank decided?
prompts.needles: rank octoverse tiobe pypl index usage blend
prompts.answer: A 2025–2026 blend of GitHub Octoverse and TIOBE/PYPL, then Ruby and Elixir added because they actually live here. Indexes move. This snapshot does not pretend to be gospel.

prompts.label: What does east mean?
prompts.needles: east year timeline drift map axis
prompts.answer: Year drifts east. Rank hangs higher. An early language sits left; a widely used one hangs nearer the top of the sky.
